page: Vultr voc-g-1c-4gb-30s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute instance featuring a dedicated AMD EPYC processor with 1 vCPU, 1 physical core, and 1 thread per core running at 2.0 GHz. The system is equipped with 4.0 GB of system memory and 30 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. The x86_64 architecture includes hardware support for AVX, AES, SHA_NI, and BMI2 instructions, alongside a cache hierarchy consisting of 32 KB L1d, 0.5 MB L2, and 32 MB L3 cache.

Benchmark results indicate strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 25%. However, due to the single-core configuration, multi-core performance is limited, scoring in the bottom 25% for both stress-ng and Geekbench multi-core tests. Memory performance is a notable bottleneck; the passmark memory score falls in the bottom 25%, and small-block cached read-only memory bandwidth is in the bottom 10% at 142.91 GB/sec. Large-block read and write bandwidths are also weak at 31.44 GB/sec and 22.58 GB/sec respectively.

This instance is suited for lightweight, single-threaded workloads such as basic text processing, single-threaded compression tasks, or small-scale web serving. It is less optimal for database operations, software compilation, or image processing, which scored in the bottom 10% of benchmarks. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated CPU allocation provides predictable single-threaded performance for entry-level workloads without the CPU credit limitations of burstable instances, though resource density is low.
